newsitem.title: UK: T-bonds firm in calm London after Friday's storm.
newsitem.headline: T-bonds firm in calm London after Friday's storm.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries firmed in calm market conditions in London on Monday after Friday's storm and were set to hold steady throughout the session, analysts said.
"It's quite firm this morning. The market wants to take the good news," a London-based trader at a European bank said.
"We've got to wait for New York to come in before the market does much more."
The benchmark 30-year long bond was trading at 100-08 to yield 6.48 percent at 1130 GMT, versus 100-03 in Tokyo and 99-27 at the close in New York on Friday.
Overnight buying from Japan provided the impetus for the day's modest gains, in addition to a higher dollar and generally buoyant European markets, traders said.
"If the Japanese continue to show up, it could hold the market in a decent shape into the year end," a trader at a Japanese bank in London said.
The overall market tone looked positive and would continue to firm slightly through year end, analysts said.
"On the upside, there's a lot of air up there. If we do start popping up, it could go up quite quickly," the European bank trader said.
Any upswing, however, would likely be countered by investors selling on upticks, traders said.
Analysts said Friday's precipitous drop was overblown and that Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comments did not signal any change in monetary policy outlook.
"The market has come to the view that reactions were exaggerated and didn't significantly change the outlook for monetary policy in the U.S.," said the European bank trader.
"Let's face it, the Fed had and still has a bias towards tightening and that is reflected in the curve," said David Hewitt, economist at Tokyo Mitsubishi.
However, the Japanese bank trader said Greenspan's comments would continue to overhang the market.

"Greenspan isn't one for misplacing his comments. He won't exactly be retracting very quickly," he said. "That will overhang the market some more." No major data is scheduled for release until Wednesday, when the November producer price index (PPI) is due, followed by the Consumer Price Index (CPI) on Thursday.

Hewitt said he expected the figures to be overall neutral for bonds. He said there might be some re-flattening of the yield curve ahead of the two- and five-year bond auctions scheduled for December 18 and 19 respectively.
March T-bond futures were at 114-11 in automated trade, up 16/32 from Friday's Chicago settlement.
